catalog_quote: 4.2.4. Syllables, word-structure and phonotactics. There is a concise summary of Aslian word-structure in Dunn et al. (2011: 300): The final syllable in most Aslian languages always has the structure /CVC/. The reason for this … is that Aslian languages, like other Mon-Khmer languages, seldom have suffixes, and the end of the word is therefore usually part of the root and not affected by synchronic or diachronic morphophonemic processes. Also, the final syllable is the most informative part of a word in that it always receives stress and contains the greatest phonemic variation. [Benjamin 2012: 187] ... Aslian languages are phonologically very conservative, retaining much that has been lost elsewhere: full pre-syllables (Diffloth 1976d: 232), ‘original’ long vowels (Central Aslian only), typically iambic sesquisyllabic (one-and-a-half-syllable) accentual patterns [Benjamin 2012: 178] ..…
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level generalization only: in Aslian languages (Sabüm included by membership in Central Aslian) the word-final 'major' syllable, always CVC, carries the stress; preceding 'minor' syllables are unstressed with reduced/predictable vowels (iambic sesquisyllabic pattern). No source states this for Sabüm itself.
new_statements.exceptions: Benjamin 2012: 187 qualifies only the CVC claim (Southern Aslian allows final CV); no exceptions to final stress are stated. Nothing on Sabüm's own polysyllables (Malay loans, reduplications).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (root/sesquisyllable), citation-form data. The statement is an Aslian-wide typological generalization in surveys (Benjamin 2012; Dunn et al. 2011, attributed to Diffloth 1976: 102 and p.c; Matisoff 2003: 11), not a description of Sabüm; the only first-hand Sabüm material (Benjamin 1976 wordlists, one speaker, 1960s) is silent on stress and the language is extinct, so no Sabüm-specific statement can ever be expected beyond Benjamin's or Diffloth's unpublished notes.
new_statements.identity_note: Sabüm (sabu1253, sbo) is an extinct 'Lanoh'-cluster Central Aslian variety of Lenggong, Upper Perak, known only from Benjamin's 1960s wordlist (one informant) and Diffloth's 1975 remarks; its closest documented relative is Semnam (semn1250; Burenhult & Wegener 2009, final-syllable stress). Benjamin 1976: 125 tentatively equates Skeat & Blagden's 1906 'Sem. Per.' (Semang of Perak) list with Sabum. The stress statement quoted is an Aslian-family generalization (Benjamin 2012, Dunn et al. 2011, Matisoff 2003), not a description of Sabüm.

sources.note: Family-level only: p. 178 Aslian retains 'typically iambic sesquisyllabic (one-and-a-half-syllable) accentual patterns'; p. 179 'major (i.e., stressed, word-final) vowel systems' and lists Sabüm among the Central Aslian languages with phonemic vowel length; p. 187 (§4.2.4) quotes Dunn et al. 2011: 300 that the final syllable 'always receives stress'. p. 166: Sabüm and Lanoh Yir 'appear to have become extinct since I recorded their vocabularies in the 1960s'. No Sabüm-specific stress remark.

sources.citation: Burenhult, Niclas & Claudia Wegener. 2009. Preliminary notes on the phonology, orthography and vocabulary of Semnam (Austroasiatic, Malay Peninsula). JSEALS 1: 283-312.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes SEMNAM (semn1250), Sabüm's closest relative, not Sabüm. p. 284: 'As in other Aslian languages, the full range of phonemes is only to be found in the last, stressed syllable of words.' Wordlist entry 'sabɨɨm [saˈbɨːᵇm] /sabɨːm/ pn. Ethnonym: Sabüm' shows final stress in the Semnam word for Sabüm.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level: p. 11 'Sesquisyllabic forms consist of a major syllable with fully-stressed vowel, preceded by a minor syllable with predictable vocalism'. Sabum-specific content is segmental only: p. 16 vowel length retained in Semai, Temiar and Sabum [Diffloth 1975:10]; pp. 19-20 Sabum final-nasal denasalization correlated with vowel length, original final stops voiced to -b -d -j -g (after Diffloth 1975).

sources.note: Nothing. The only first-hand Sabüm material in print: 146-item lexicostatistical wordlists from one informant ('SABUM: Layan d/o Buloh, Lenggong, Perak', p. 127); Sabum 'a Lanoh subgroup; Negritos belonging to a nearly extinct group.. near Lenggong' (p. 48); Semnam and Sabum 'separated out from Lanoh proper' (p. 45); tentatively equates Skeat & Blagden's 'Sem. Per.' list with Sabum (p. 125, '?Sabum'). Full scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: no hit.
